summary: Interpreted the constructor-replay receipt and closed that question, then filed the FSM-divergence successor for the cluster question. Receipt 00386ad8ea534d91a0ef7506fabc9527 parsed all eight events and evaluated all five comparisons: with the replay enabled the constructor did not return within the window at both scales (witnesses at indices 3 and 7 — 141 batches from 9000 entries at MaxAppendEntries 64, and 200 batches from only 200 committed entries at MaxAppendEntries 1), while both feature-off controls over identical fixtures returned with lastApplied still at the snapshot index (holds at indices 1 and 5, control operand at 1, channel capacity 128 observed at 1). The experiment-level interpretation is violated/asserted with those indices and the question-level account is explained/asserted, with the mechanism traced through restoreFromCommittedLogs → processLogs → fsmMutateCh and runFSM being started only after the constructor returns; limits kept are the supplied fixture, no live node producing the gap, the 5 s window with the source argument for permanence, and the unrecovered stalled constructor. A new fact records the trigger bound (129 entries at MaxAppendEntries 1, 8193 at the default 64, no-op entries excluded) with the receipt as execution. Finally I extended the cluster harness to sample each node's applied FSM commands after healing — deterministic in local repeats: A and C applied minority-write while B, D and E applied majority-write with all nodes at log index 13 — and filed that as a successor of the healing-phase experiment with three comparisons over the applied-state divergence, leaving the ten earlier comparisons with their own receipt. Incomplete: that receipt and interpretation, the no-feature restart control, and the long-run/repair-path window.
